title: How to Cook Quinoa So It Turns Out Fluffy

seo.title: How to Cook Quinoa So It Turns Out Fluffy
seo.meta_description: Rinse, use about 1 part quinoa to 1.75–2 parts water, simmer gently until absorbed, then rest covered before fluffing with a fork.
seo.search_intent: Cook quinoa with separate grains instead of a wet or mushy texture.

excerpt: For fluffy quinoa, water control matters more than stirring. Start around 1 part quinoa to 1.75–2 parts liquid, simmer until absorbed, then let it rest covered for 5–10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
content_html:
Overcooked quinoa can turn wet and porridge-like. Properly cooked quinoa keeps distinct seeds with the tiny spiral germ visible. The main trick is using no more water than the seeds can absorb and giving them a final rest.

1. Rinse if needed

A quick rinse removes residual saponins. Drain well so unmeasured water does not follow the quinoa into the pot.

2. Use a moderate water ratio

A useful starting point is 1 cup quinoa to 1.75–2 cups water. Pre-rinsed or wetter quinoa may need slightly less.

3. Simmer rather than boil hard

Bring to a boil, lower the heat, cover, and cook about 12–15 minutes until liquid is absorbed and the germ separates visibly.

4. Rest before fluffing

Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 5–10 minutes. Then fluff with a fork.

If it is still wet

Uncover and cook briefly over very low heat. If the quinoa is already soft and there is lots of liquid, the original water ratio was too high.

Fluffy quinoa is an absorption method finished with steam—not something that improves with constant stirring.

faq.question: How much water does quinoa need?
faq.answer: A good starting point is about 1.75–2 parts water for 1 part quinoa.

faq.question: How long does quinoa cook?
faq.answer: Usually about 12–15 minutes plus a 5–10 minute covered rest.

faq.question: Should quinoa be stirred?
faq.answer: Not constantly. Combine it at the start and fluff it with a fork at the end.
